newsitem.title: ITALY: U.S. forces rescue 85 Albanians in Adriatic.
newsitem.headline: U.S. forces rescue 85 Albanians in Adriatic.

text.p: U.S. forces rescued 85 Albanians from two stricken boats in the Adriatic, including one with 55 people aboard which capsized and sank, a U.S. Navy spokesman said on Monday.

The spokesman, Lieutenant Commander William Fenick, said both rescues took place on Sunday evening off the coast of Albania, where a Marine expeditionary unit is spearheading the evacuation of U.S. and other nationals from the country's chaos.

Fenick said the amphibious assault ship USS Nassau, command ship of the unit, had received a distress call from the first Albanian vessel saying it had 55 men on board and that it was taking on water after engine trouble.
He said 23 Marine and Navy swimmers, on one of six rescue boats involved in the helicopter-assisted operation, went into action when the Albanian vessel began to capsize.

"The swimmers recovered the men in the water as the boat capsized. We recovered all 55 of the Albanians that were in the water," Fenick, a spokesman for the U.S. Sixth Fleet, said by telephone from Gaeta, Italy.
He said a second Albanian vessel with 30 men on board later pulled alongside the Nassau and asked for help.
"It was overcrowded and we decided it was in the best interest to help so they climbed a ladder to get on board," Fenick said.
He said all 85 Albanians remained on the Nassau while higher authorities decide when and where they should be put ashore.
Some 6,000 Albanians, fleeing the unrest in their homeland, have reached Italy this month in a ramschackle flotilla of boats, many of them unseaworthy and badly overcrowded.
